findings.title: Paid-booking cancellation returns before workflow reminders are cancelled
findings.body: For a paid booking the handler takes the `bookingToDelete.paid` branch (starts at line 363), refunds, sets status REJECTED, and returns at this line. The workflow reminder cancellation block (lines 484-493) and the zapier `cancelScheduledJobs` call come after this return, so they never run for paid bookings. The booking is cancelled, but its scheduled BEFORE_EVENT email and SMS reminders are still sent, which is the exact bug this PR is meant to fix. The same gap exists at line 437 (`return null` when the payment service is not implemented), and any throw between the status update at line 255 and line 484 leaves reminders uncancelled. Reminder cancellation should happen before the paid branch, or be duplicated into it.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and skips all deletes
findings.body: The loop awaits `client.request` for every cancelled reminder inside a single try block. If any call throws (for example SendGrid rejects a batch that was already sent or already cancelled), the catch at lines 75-77 runs and the loop is abandoned, so the remaining reminders in the window are never cancelled. Also, `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` returns a lazy PrismaPromise that only executes when awaited in `Promise.all` at line 74. Because that await is never reached after an error, the deletes for reminders already cancelled earlier in the loop never run either. Those rows keep `cancelled: true`, and the next cron run (about 15 minutes later) hits the same failing reminder first. A single bad batch therefore blocks cancellation of every other reminder in its one-hour window, and emails for cancelled bookings still go out. Each cancel should be isolated (try/catch per reminder), and the delete should be awaited right after its own successful cancel.

findings.title: Immediate cancel path reuses the call that hits SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellation cap
findings.body: The `immediateDelete` branch sends `status: "cancel"` to SendGrid's `/v3/user/scheduled_sends`. The PR description identifies this exact mechanism as the root cause: each cancelled send stays pending until its scheduled date, and once 100 are pending new cancels fail while the emails are still sent. This branch is used for rescheduling (handleNewBooking.ts line 968), workflow deletion (workflows.tsx line 214) and step deletion (workflows.tsx line 521), which can cancel many reminders at once. When the cap is hit, the error is swallowed by the catch at the bottom of the function, so the reminders are silently still sent. The branch also returns without touching the DB row, so the reminder keeps `scheduled: true` and a `referenceId` pointing at a cancelled batch until its scheduled date passes. The name `immediateDelete` is also misleading because the row is not deleted. These paths should use the same deferred `cancelled` flag and cron-based cancellation as the rest of the PR.

findings.title: Cancellation flag write is fire-and-forget, so the reminder's fate is not guaranteed
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is async, but it is called without `await` here (and the same pattern appears in bookings.tsx line 490 and workflows.tsx). The `cancelled: true` UPDATE that now decides whether the reminder is sent may not complete before the handler returns, and on a serverless runtime the process can be frozen after the response. Errors are swallowed inside the helper's try/catch, so a failed write leaves the booking cancelled with no record that its reminder must be stopped, and nothing retries it. The helper's result should be awaited and failures surfaced or retried.

findings.title: SMS reminder row is only deleted if the Twilio cancel succeeds
findings.body: The Prisma `workflowReminder.delete` runs after `twilio.cancelSMS` in the same try block. If Twilio throws (for example because the message is already sent or no longer cancellable), the delete is skipped and the error is only logged. Before this change the callers deleted the row regardless of the Twilio result, so this is a regression: the row keeps `scheduled: true` and its `referenceId`. The row deletion should not depend on the external cancel succeeding.

findings.title: Cron endpoint authorizes everyone when CRON_API_KEY is unset
findings.body: If `CRON_API_KEY` is not configured and the request has neither an `authorization` header nor an `apiKey` query parameter, `apiKey` is `undefined` and the check `process.env.CRON_API_KEY !== apiKey` evaluates to `undefined !== undefined`, which is false, so the request proceeds. This is pre-existing, but the endpoint now also cancels SendGrid sends and deletes reminder rows, so an unauthenticated caller on a misconfigured deployment can trigger those side effects. The handler should reject when the key is missing.

findings.title: Unrelated UI restructuring bundled into a reminder-cancellation fix
findings.body: The condition changes from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded` and the phone block is unwrapped. This changes rendering for SMS_ATTENDEE steps, which no longer get an empty padded container. Nothing in the PR description or title mentions this UI change, and it is unrelated to cancelling reminders. It should be split into its own PR or described explicitly.

findings.title: New cancel-and-delete cron logic and cancelled flag have no tests
findings.body: The PR changes cancellation semantics across handleCancelBooking, bookings.tsx, handleNewBooking and workflows.tsx, adds a `cancelled` column with a migration, and adds a cron branch that calls SendGrid and deletes rows. None of this is covered by a test in the diff. The previous fix shipped broken with the failure silently swallowed. At minimum, tests should cover: a cancelled reminder inside the one-hour window being cancelled and deleted; a SendGrid failure for one reminder not blocking the others; and a paid booking's reminders being cancelled.
